summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Lockroy, the stage name of Joseph-Philippe Simon. Born in Turin to Baron General Henri Simon, who opposed an artistic career for his son, he acted under the name Lockroy at the Odéon-Théâtre de l'Europe and the Comédie-Française before turning fully to writing. In 1848 he briefly served as provisional administrator of the Comédie-Française.
one_line: Lockroy, born Joseph-Philippe Simon in Turin, was a French actor turned writer who briefly administered the Comédie-Française in 1848.
key_facts: Joseph-Philippe Simon was born in Turin.
Joseph-Philippe Simon was the son of Baron General Henri Simon.
Baron General Henri Simon forbade his son's use of his surname in an artistic career.
Joseph-Philippe Simon began his acting career under the pseudonym Lockroy.
Lockroy first acted at the Odéon-Théâtre de l'Europe in Paris.
Lockroy also acted at the Comédie-Française in Paris.
Lockroy devoted himself entirely to writing after his acting career.
For a few months in 1848, Lockroy served as provisional administrator of the Comédie-Française.
